title: Pastoral Care
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Pastoral care is the shepherding ministry of teaching, prayer, correction, comfort, protection, and patient care for souls within the church. It reflects Christ’s care for His sheep through faithful servants.
summary: Pastoral care is the shepherding ministry of teaching, prayer, correction, comfort, protection, and patient care for souls within the church. It reflects Christ’s care for His sheep through faithful servants.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd who knows, feeds, leads, restores, and keeps His sheep. Pastoral care is faithful only when it reflects His truth, compassion, holiness, and patience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The people of God need shepherding. Pastoral care is more than public preaching or organizational management. It includes watching over souls, feeding the flock, protecting the vulnerable, correcting the wandering, and comforting the afflicted.

Faithful pastoral care is shaped by Christ’s own shepherd heart. He seeks the lost, restores the straying, strengthens the weak, and lays down His life for the sheep.

Pastoral care also requires truth. Compassion without Scripture can become sentimentality, while correction without compassion can become harshness. Christlike care brings truth and mercy together.

This ministry is not limited to pastors alone, though leaders carry special responsibility. The whole church shares in mutual care, encouragement, prayer, and burden-bearing under faithful shepherding.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have been harmed by neglectful, harsh, or self-protective leadership. Biblical pastoral care shows a better pattern: shepherds who serve under Christ for the good of souls.

This doctrine also matters for the weak and wounded. Christ’s church should not abandon sheep who are suffering, confused, tempted, disabled, recovering, or grieving.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Seek and support Christlike shepherding in the church. If you are entrusted with care, move toward people with truth, patience, prayer, and compassion. If you need care, do not suffer silently; ask faithful believers and leaders to walk with you under the care of Christ.
